examples: `new Written` stores three values and calls nothing; a program meets a `Written` as the result of `Workbook::finish`, whose examples read every one of them.
perf: `new Written` stores three values and calls nothing; `Workbook::finish` builds one on every call, so its figure includes this one.
hostile: `new Written` stores three typed read-only values and calls nothing, so a wrong value does not compile and there is no input left to attack.
